name: Python Trivia
description: Monty Python, the Zen of Python, walruses and "what does this print?" — fun trivia about the world's friendliest language.
question: {prompt}

cards.fact: Guido started Python as a hobby project over the Christmas holidays of 1989 in the Netherlands.

options: Python, the serpent of Greek myth
cards.fact: Guido was reading the Monty Python scripts and wanted a name that was short, unique and slightly mysterious.

cards.prompt: In which year was Python first released publicly?
cards.fact: Version 0.9.0 was posted to the Usenet group alt.sources in February 1991.

cards.prompt: Guido van Rossum's nickname "BDFL" stands for…
cards.fact: Guido stepped down from the role in July 2018; Python is now steered by an elected council.

cards.prompt: In which year was Python 3.0 released?
cards.fact: Python 3 deliberately broke backward compatibility to fix long-standing design warts.

cards.prompt: Python 2 officially reached end of life in…
cards.fact: Python 2.7 was sunset on 1 January 2020, after an extra five years of support.

cards.prompt: The standard Python interpreter, CPython, is written mainly in…
cards.fact: Other implementations exist too: Jython runs on the JVM and PyPy is written in Python itself.

cards.prompt: What happens when you run import antigravity?
cards.answer: It opens the xkcd "Python" comic in your browser
options: It disables gravity in turtle graphics
cards.fact: The Easter egg points to xkcd #353, in which a character flies after "import antigravity".

cards.prompt: Which line prints "The Zen of Python"?
cards.fact: The Zen is 19 aphorisms, starting with "Beautiful is better than ugly."
It was published as PEP 20; Tim Peters left a 20th aphorism for Guido to fill in, which he never did.

cards.answer: The style guide for Python code
cards.fact: PEP 8 is why Python code favours 4-space indents and snake_case names.

cards.prompt: Python's standard package installer is called…
cards.fact: pip is a recursive acronym: "pip installs packages".

cards.prompt: Where are public Python packages published?
cards.fact: PyPI was once nicknamed "the Cheese Shop", after a Monty Python sketch.

cards.prompt: What does Python use to mark blocks of code?
cards.fact: Indentation is part of the syntax, so Python code always looks tidy.

cards.prompt: What is Python's "nothing here" value called?
cards.fact: None is a singleton, so the idiomatic test is "x is None".

cards.prompt: By convention, the first parameter of an instance method is named…
cards.fact: self is only a convention, but nearly every Python programmer follows it.
Short anonymous functions use lambda instead.

cards.prompt: In Python slang, a "dunder" method is one named with…
cards.fact: Dunder methods let your own classes work with operators, len(), print() and more.
Because tuples cannot change, they can be used as dictionary keys.

cards.prompt: What does the interactive Python prompt look like?
cards.fact: Continuation lines in the interactive shell show "..." instead.
The GIL lets only one thread run Python bytecode at a time; Python 3.13 added an experimental build without it.
It arrived in Python 3.8 (PEP 572); turn your head sideways to see the walrus.

cards.prompt: Which Python version introduced f-strings like f"Hi {name}"?
cards.fact: f-strings came from PEP 498 and are now the most popular way to format text.

cards.prompt: Which Python version added the match statement (structural pattern matching)?
cards.fact: Pattern matching was specified in PEPs 634–636.

cards.prompt: In Python 2, print was a statement. In Python 3 it became…
cards.fact: That is why Python 3 needs parentheses: print("hello").
Multiplying a string by a number repeats it.
// is floor division: it rounds down to a whole number.
** is exponentiation, so this is 2 to the power of 10.
A slice step of -1 walks the string backwards.
Empty containers are "falsy", which is why "if my_list:" checks for items.
Binary floating point cannot store 0.1 exactly; the sum is 0.30000000000000004.
Negative indexes count from the end of the list.

cards.prompt: What does this print in Python 3?
cards.fact: In Python 2 this printed 0; Python 3 made / always return a float.
join is a string method: the separator goes first.
range stops before its end value, so range(3) gives 0, 1 and 2.
sorted() always returns a list, even when given a string.
split() with no arguments breaks a string on whitespace, giving ['hello', 'world'].
